title: Pill Group
description: Public API, selection modes, state timing, accessibility, validation, and platform behaviour for Firstlight Pill Group.

blocks.text: Pill Group presents compact, individually shaped options for selecting zero or one value, or zero or more values.
Single selection is the default:

<firstlight:pill-group
    :options="$queueOptions"
    native:model="queue"
    label="Queue"
    helper="Choose the queue to include."
/>
Use multiple with an array-valued property:
public array $queues = ['mine'];

<firstlight:pill-group
    :options="$queueOptions"
    native:model="queues"
    label="Queues"
    helper="Choose any that apply."
    multiple
/>

blocks.label: options
blocks.text:
Accepted type: array
Purpose: Simple strings, a value-to-label map, or rich option arrays.

blocks.label: value / native:model
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string, int, array, or null
Purpose: Stable selection. Use a scalar or null in single mode and a homogeneous list or null in multiple mode.

blocks.label: multiple
blocks.text:
Accepted type: bool
Purpose: Enables zero-or-more selection. Defaults to false.

blocks.label: label
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Visible field label.

blocks.label: helper
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Supporting text below the pills.

blocks.label: error
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Error text and native error semantics.

blocks.label: required
blocks.text:
Accepted type: bool
Purpose: Communicates required state; PHP still owns validation.

blocks.label: disabled
blocks.text:
Accepted type: bool
Purpose: Disables the complete group.

blocks.label: a11y-label
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Explicit accessibility label when a visible label is inappropriate.

blocks.label: a11y-hint
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Additional VoiceOver and TalkBack guidance.

blocks.label: class
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: External EDGE layout utilities.
Simple strings use the same value and label:
['Mine', 'All']
A map separates stable values from labels and may use all-string or all-integer keys:
['mine' => 'Mine', 'all' => 'All']
Rich options accept only value, label, and optional disabled fields:

[
    ['value' => 'mine', 'label' => 'Mine'],
    ['value' => 'all', 'label' => 'All', 'disabled' => true],
]

All values in one group must be unique and must all be strings or all be integers. In single mode, tapping the selected pill proposes null. In multiple mode, tapping toggles that stable value while preserving the order of the others. null and [] both mean no multiple selection.
@change receives the complete proposed selection: a scalar or null in single mode and a list in multiple mode. native:model normally generates this callback for property synchronisation.

Pill Group is server-authoritative. A tap emits immediately, but selected visuals wait for PHP's next publication. Further taps are ignored while that proposal is in flight so a rapid second tap cannot be calculated from stale state. Programmatic updates and reconciliation do not emit.
Use plain native:model or native:model.live; deferred blur and debounce modes are rejected.
disabled prevents every pill from emitting. A rich option's disabled: true affects only that pill. An empty option set becomes an inert disabled group.
required is metadata rather than client-side enforcement. It does not prevent clearing the final pill; validate the resulting value in PHP and publish error when needed.

Provide either a visible label or an explicit a11y-label. Firstlight warns during development when both are blank. Each pill exposes its label, selected state, and disabled state through native platform semantics. Selection also has a visible checkmark, so it does not depend on colour alone. Pills wrap at larger text sizes and retain at least a 44-point iOS or 48-dp Android interaction target.

Contract exceptions still reject malformed options, mixed selections, and
unsupported presentation props before publication. User validation is
separate: screens that use ValidatesFields auto-bind the first MessageBag
message for the field's native:model or error-for name. An authored
error wins. required is display metadata and does not run Laravel rules.
See Validate fields. A same-typed selected
value absent from options remains unselected rather than selecting a
fallback.

iOS uses native SwiftUI capsule buttons in a wrapping layout. Android uses Material 3 FilterChip controls in a wrapping FlowRow. Both inherit NativePHP semantic theme tokens and preserve native press, focus, selection, disabled, and accessibility behaviour without exposing platform-widget props.
Pill Group supports the versions listed in the current compatibility reference and requires both native renderers to be compiled into the host application.
